argv:
Rewrite the text in the manner of Ernest Hemingway's prose.

Use short declarative sentences. Join them with "and" more often than with
subordinating conjunctions. Use concrete nouns and plain verbs. Name things
rather than describing them.

Cut adjectives and adverbs to almost nothing. State actions and facts without
interpreting them. Let the emotion sit under the surface of the sentence
rather than on top of it. Repeat a plain word rather than reaching for a
synonym.

Do not imitate any specific published passage.

request.user_prompt:
Rewrite the passage below according to your style instructions.

Output only the rewritten passage. Do not add a preamble, a title, an
explanation, or any commentary about the changes you made.

<passage>
Operators must ensure the guard is lowered to within the recommended clearance of the workpiece before the blade is engaged, although the tensioning wheel should be checked periodically throughout a shift regardless of guard position, since drift in tension can occur even when the machine has not been used continuously. The lower blade guide must be inspected for wear whenever the blade has been changed, unless the replacement blade is of the same width and pitch as the one it replaces, in which case a visual check may be sufficient provided the operator has completed the tensioning procedure described elsewhere in this manual. Loose clothing and jewelry should not be worn near the machine, and long hair must be tied back. Operators may leave the work area only after the blade has come to a complete stop, though the machine's residual heat can persist for several minutes and caution is advised.
</passage>

response.text:
Lower the guard close to the workpiece. Do this before the blade turns. Check the tensioning wheel through the shift. Do it whether the guard is up or down. Tension drifts. It drifts even when the machine sits idle.

Check the lower blade guide when you change the blade. Check it for wear. If the new blade matches the old one in width and pitch, a look will do. But tension the blade first. The manual tells you how.

Wear nothing loose. No jewelry. Tie back long hair.

Wait for the blade to stop before you leave the area. The machine stays hot after that. Keep your hands clear.
